newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - BTPs overbought,seen correcting to 132.76.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - BTPs overbought,seen correcting to 132.76.

text.p: September BTPs were slightly overbought in early trade on Thursday and needed to pull back to around 132.76 before the market could go on to test new highs, technical analysts said.
"Near term it's probably a bit overdone," said Robin Wilkin, senior technical analyst at MCM YieldWatch here.
"We're looking for some corrective pull back or sideways action...ahead of another move higher."
By 0818 GMT, September BTPs were up 51 basis points at 133.59 and the relative strength index was at 72.4 percent. A reading above 70 percent indicates a contract is overbought.

Wilkin said any pull-back would find support around 133.02 then 132.76, the 38 and 62 percent retracements of the latest rally from the 132.31 low on Wednesday to an intra-day high at 133.47 earlier on Thursday.
"But there are no real signs of a top forming. After this correction we may see a move to 134.61, the Fibonacci projection of the move from 128.60, the low on May 30," said Wilkin.

But he added that a weak close on Thursday, below 132.76, would open up the potential for a move back to around 132.00, then 131.78. This is the 38 percent retracement of the rally from the June 10 low at 129.07 to 133.47.
Richard Adcock, technical research manager at HSBC Futures here, said any weakness in BTPs offered a buying opportunity.

"At this time with momentum still rising in a very bullish way, there seems little to stand in the way of the advance," he said in a note for clients. "This suggests weakness continues to offer buying opportunities looking for moves up to 133.75 and on further in time."
He said to the downside, stops should be placed under 132.50.
By 0845 GMT, September Eurolira was up three basis points at 93.46.
